Magbish
MAG-bish
proper noun
Hebrew magbish, perhaps “congregating” or “gathering,” a town or company of Judah whose men returned from the captivity in Babylon.

Biblical Definition

Magbish is named but once in all the Scripture, in the register of those who came up out of the captivity of Babylon, where an hundred fifty and six of its children are numbered among the remnant of Zerubbabel’s company (Ezr 2:30). Whether it was a town of Judah or a family reckoned by their head, the dictionary will not feign to know where the LORD was pleased to record only the name and the number; yet the name itself, perhaps signifying “gathering,” falls fitly upon a people gathered home from a far land. For this was the great work of that hour, that the LORD, having sent His people into Babylon for their sins, should turn again their captivity and gather them by the proclamation of Cyrus, whose spirit He had stirred. The men of Magbish are not named in Nehemiah’s parallel list, so that this once-spoken name might easily have perished from memory; but the Spirit of God set it down, that not one company of the returning should be unremembered. Magbish stands as a witness that the providence of God gathers His scattered people one band at a time, and counts each into His book; and it points beyond itself to the great gathering, when the Lord shall gather together His elect from the four winds, and not one of all whom the Father hath given Him shall be lost.

Webster 1828 Definition

A town or company of Judah whose hundred fifty and six men returned from the captivity in Babylon.

MAGBISH, a town or family of Judah, perhaps signifying “gathering.”

Its children are numbered among the returnees from Babylon.

An hundred fifty and six of its men are reckoned in the register.

The name appears but once in all the Scripture, in the book of the return.

It witnesses to the LORD’s gathering of His scattered people band by band.

Key Scripture

Ezr 2:30 — "The children of Magbish, an hundred fifty and six."

Ezr 1:1 — "Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing, saying,"

Psa 126:1 — "When the LORD turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream."

Mat 24:31 — "And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other."

Modern Corruption

A name of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to the LORD’s gathering of His scattered people band by band.

expand to see more

Magbish is a name of the sacred register of the return, spoken but once, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the reader who meets the name among the returnees may know it for a real company brought home by a real God who turned again the captivity of His people.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the gathering mercy of God toward His scattered remnant. He who counted the hundred fifty and six of Magbish in the book of the return is the same who shall send His angels to gather His elect from the four winds. The saint who fears to be overlooked in the great multitude may remember Magbish, a name spoken but once, yet kept for ever in the record of the LORD’s gathering of His own.

Hebrew Roots

Perhaps from a Hebrew root meaning “gathering,” Magbish names a company among the returnees from Babylon.

Usage

"Like the children of Magbish, each band of the returning remnant is gathered and counted by the LORD."

"The God who turned again the captivity of Zion gathers His scattered people one company at a time."

"A name spoken but once in Scripture is yet kept for ever in the record of the great gathering home."
